title: Dashboard signal symphony and trace pivots — planning notes
content:
Context and intent:

This is a planning / sketch doc to propose a coherent signal set and trace pivot strategy for the operator-facing dashboards we need for the upcoming Dedicated + Private rollout. Goal: make investigation fast, reduce query cost, and provide clear handoffs between SRE, serving-runtime, and product-ops. This is intentionally pragmatic — a mix of high-level taxonomy plus concrete metric definitions and small widget-level rules.

Audience: oncall engineers, dashboard owners, release lead for dedicated rollout (Samira), and anyone instrumenting models or routing policies.

Design principles (short):
- One signal, one intent: every dashboard panel must answer a single question (e.g., "is KV cache warming?" not "is anything weird?").
- Cost-aware instrumentation: prioritize low-cardinality rollups + traces for high-severity anomalies only.
- Trace pivots tied to metric anchors: traces must be linkable from metric rows via deterministic keys (session_id, request_id, tenant_id).
- Fast path for triage: default dashboard should surface 3 hypotheses (latency, cold-cache, model-change) and provide 1-click pivots to traces or probe logs.

Signal taxonomy (rough):
- Health signals (global): cluster_utilization_pct, node_gpu_mem_used_bytes, gpus_available_count
- Latency signals (user-facing): ttf_token_p50_ms, ttf_token_p95_ms, first_chunk_latency_ms
- Cost signals: tokens_served_per_min, amortized_gpu_sec_per_1000_tokens, batch_size_median
- Cache / warm signals: kv_prefetch_hit_rate, kv_eviction_rate_per_min, prefix_warmth_index
- Quality signals: latents_hallucination_rate_est, rerank_confidence_pct (note: derived from evals)
- Control-plane signals: model_fanout_errors_count, routing_fallback_rate_pct

Concrete metric definitions (for instrumentation and dashboard panels):
(plain text rows so these can be copy/pasted into metric-defs spreadsheet)

metric_name | type | unit | aggregation | owner | short_description | alert_hint
cluster_utilization_pct | gauge | percent | avg over 1m | infra | GPU utilization across serving cluster | SRE: sustained > 85%
ttf_token_p95_ms | histogram-derived | ms | p95 over 1m | serving-runtime | time-to-first-token 95th percentile | product: p95 > 250ms
kv_prefetch_hit_rate | ratio | pct | weighted avg over 5m | serving-runtime | fraction of requests served from KV prefix cache | ops: drop > 60%
prefix_warmth_index | derived | unitless 0-1 | 5m rolling | eng-observability | heuristic: fraction of recent prefixes observed in last 5m | useful for cold-start triage
model_fanout_errors_count | counter | count | sum over 1m | routing | count of fanout failures (partial model list) | critical if > 1 and correlated with client errors

Notes on prefix_warmth_index: this is intentionally a fuzzy signal — combine with kv_prefetch_hit_rate and ttf_token_p50_ms. Implementation suggestion: maintain probabilistic TTL set keyed by (tenant_id, model_variant) with exponential decay to avoid cardinality explosion.

Trace pivot policy (how dashboards link to traces):
- Primary pivot keys: request_id (preferred), if not available then session_id + tenant_id + timestamp_bucket.
- Sample rates: baseline 0.1% of successful requests, 100% of traces when alerting threshold breached for a tenant or model variant.
- Severity-weighted capture: increase sampling to 5% for requests with ttf_token > p95 or kv_prefetch_miss.
- Trace enrichment: include minimal prompt slice (first 256 chars), model_variant, routing_path, batch_size, kv_hit boolean, host_id. Must strip user PHI before retention.

Dashboard composition proposals (wireframe notes):
- Top row: global health (cluster_utilization_pct, gpus_available_count, tokens_served_per_min) + one-line operational status (current incidents, probe success rate).
- Second row: latency panel (ttf_token_p50/p95, first_chunk_latency_ms) with heatmap by tenant weight and small sparkline of kv_prefetch_hit_rate.
- Third row: cache state (kv_prefetch_hit_rate, prefix_warmth_index, kv_eviction_rate_per_min) with a drilldown table showing top-20 tenants by miss rate and per-tenant probe status.
- Right rail: quick-actions and pivots (collect-trace, re-run-probe, force-warm-prefix). Buttons call infra-runbooks endpoints.

Widget heuristics and sizing (small ops-focused rules):
- Avoid high-cardinality group-bys by default. Provide a single dropdown to switch to per-tenant view (default: cluster-level).
- Heatmaps bucketization: use log-scale buckets for token volumes to avoid dominance of large tenants.
- Sparklines: 1m/5m/1h windows selectable; default 5m for operator dashboard.
- Alert context: panels must include the last correlated trace id and a copyable query for raw logs.

Probe orchestration notes (for synthetic probes used as canaries):
- Probe types: short prompt (10 tokens) for ttf check, multi-chunk probe for throughput, prefix-warm probe for KV path.
- Cadence: 30s for cluster-level short probes, 2m for per-region probes, 10m for per-tenant warm probes (only on higher tiers).
- Failure modes: record probe-level trace_id and mapping to runtime host. Probes must be labeled with probe_id and run_id.

Sampling and cost tradeoffs (practical):
- Default metrics: high cardinality tags (customer_ids, prompt_hash) are banned at 1s ingest — only allowed at rollup or sampling endpoints.
- Trace storage tiers: hot (30d) for sampled traces with alerts, warm (90d) for median traces, cold (365d) aggregated summaries only.
- Query cost mitigation: precompute per-tenant daily aggregates for top N tenants, funnel others into "long tail" buckets.

Operations playbook (compact):
- Step 1: if latency spike, check ttf_token_p95 and kv_prefetch_hit_rate. If kv hit rate dropped, run prefix-warm probe.
- Step 2: pivot to traces using request_id from the metric row. If trace sampling is low, trigger on-demand capture for 5 minutes for that tenant.
- Step 3: check model_fanout_errors_count and routing_fallback_rate_pct for correlated errors; if present, escalate to routing team.

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Do we roll our own prefix_warmth index with approximate structures or rely on a dedicated prefix service telemetry? (cost vs. accuracy)
- How aggressive should per-tenant trace capture be for premium customers? SLA-aligned?
- Do we automatically warm prefixes on detection, or only after manual approval? (safety and cost concerns)

Immediate action items (owners + near-term timeline):
- Evan: prototype prefix_warmth_index implementation using Count-Min + TTL (due 2026-02-01).
- Samira: draft dashboard wireframe in the observability dashboard board and iterate with SRE (due 2026-01-29).
- Diego: add enrichment keys to trace schema and ensure prompt scrubber pipeline is wired (due 2026-02-05).

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Consider "symptom tags" on metrics (cache-cold, model-swap, network-queue) so operator can filter quickly.
- Maybe provide a compact "incident starter" that pre-populates a ticket with correlated metric snapshot + one trace id.

References and links (copyable):
- Telemetry infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/198
- Design doc: Confluence page (linked above) with event model sketch
- Related ticket: INF-413 (rollout telemetry backlog)

If this looks reasonable I want to:
- lock the core metric names (cluster_utilization_pct, ttf_token_p95_ms, kv_prefetch_hit_rate, prefix_warmth_index) so teams have stable contracts for dashboards and alerts.
- schedule an alignment session (30m) with SRE + serving-runtime next week to finalize sampling rules.

-- Lina (notes, rough)
